:::{#thm-cross-entropy-continuous}
#### Cross-entropy of two densities

Let $X$ be a [continuous random variable](random-variables.qmd#def-continuous-rv) with [density](random-variables.qmd#def-pdf) $p$ on its [range](random-variables.qmd#def-range) $\rangef{X}$,
and let $q$ be a density on $\rangef{X}$,
with $q(x) > 0$ wherever $p(x) > 0$.
Then the [cross-entropy](#def-cross-entropy) is

$$\crossentropyf{p}{q} = -\int_{x \in \rangef{X}} p(x) \log q(x) \, dx.$$

The integrand is taken to be $0$ where $p(x) = 0$.
If instead $X$ takes a value with $q(x) = 0$ with positive [probability](probability-basics.qmd#def-probability),
both sides are $\infty$, by the same argument as in @thm-cross-entropy-discrete.

:::

::: proof

Let $g(x) \eqdef -\log q(x)$,
so that $-\log q(X) = g(X)$.
Then [LOTUS](#thm-lotus) gives

$$
\ba
\crossentropyf{p}{q}
&= \E{g(X)} && \text{(definition)} \\
&= \int_{x \in \rangef{X}} g(x) \cd p(x) \, dx && \text{(LOTUS)} \\
&= -\int_{x \in \rangef{X}} p(x) \log q(x) \, dx. && \text{(definition of } g \text{)}
\ea
$$

:::
